title: Comparison of DLIR-H and ASIR algorithms for image reconstruction in low-dose chest CT of pediatric mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia: a cross-sectional study.
summary: The study compared deep-learning-based image reconstruction (DLIR-H) with ASIR on low-dose pediatric chest CT, reporting image-quality and diagnostic performance measures in children with Mycoplasma pneumonia; this is a specific imaging result.
ai_technology: Deep-learning reconstruction DLIR-H reconstructs low-dose pediatric chest CT images for comparison with adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction (ASIR).

evidence.tested: In 142 children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia, DLIR-H had lower background noise and higher lesion contrast-to-noise ratio than ASIR-80%; radiologists gave it the highest subjective image-quality score.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective single-vendor study; lung-parenchyma SNR was lower with DLIR-H, diagnostic accuracy was not assessed, and prospective multicenter validation is needed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep-learning reconstruction DLIR-H reconstructs low-dose pediatric chest CT images for comparison with adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction (ASIR).

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
